fuite_debut.title: Leaving
fuite_debut.text:
No one stops you.

That's almost worse.

Aryn lowers her eyes.
Taera takes a step toward you, then stops.
Vael keeps his hands in his pockets.
Ikar doesn't move.

Your black blade hangs from your hand.

It is lighter than usual.

Or maybe that's you.

**"I have to go."**

You don't know whether you're saying it to them.

Or to yourself.

Aryn nods slowly.

**"I know."**

And it hurts.

Because she seems to have known for a long time.

fuite_aryn.title: Aryn
fuite_aryn.text:
Aryn steps closer.

Not too close.

Just close enough that you can hear her voice without the others hearing everything.

**"Leaving doesn't mean you have to disappear."**

You almost laugh.

Not because it's funny.

Because it's a line Aryn would say.

The kind of line that tries to open a door
without ever forcing the handle.

**"If you want to come back..."**

She stops.

She corrects herself.

**"When you want to come back."**

You don't answer.

She understands anyway.

fuite_ikar.title: Ikar
fuite_ikar.text:
Ikar says nothing.

That's rare.

No, actually.

It's Ikar.

But this silence is not the same.

He looks at your black blade.

Then his own.

Then the ground.

**"I'm sorry."**

Again.

The same words.

Less violent than his blade at your throat.

Heavier.

You want to answer him.

Tell him you understand.
Or that you don't understand.
Or that you're angry with him.
Or that you don't know.

Nothing comes out.

Ikar nods as though your silence were an answer.

Maybe it is one.

taera_derniere_main.title: The Last Hand
taera_derniere_main.text:
Taera finally steps forward.

She holds something out to you.

A small pouch.

Earth.

**"Not from my village."** she says.
**"From here."**
**"So you have a place to come back to."**

You stare at her hand.

You could take it.

You could also refuse.

Vael coughs behind her.

**"For the record, free gifts are rare."**
**"Especially ones full of dust."**

Taera shoots him a look.

He shrugs.

**"What? It's nice dust."**

You smile despite yourself.

Just for an instant.

vael_phrase.title: Vael's Line
vael_phrase.text:
Vael walks with you for a few steps.

Not far.

Just far enough to pretend this isn't a goodbye.

**"Right."** he says.
**"I'm going to say something very profound."**

He takes a breath.

Very seriously.

**"Avoid inns with signs shaped like ducks."**

You look at him.

**"That's your profound line?"**

**"No."**
**"That was genuine advice."**

He smiles.

Then his smile barely moves.

**"The profound line is: when you get tired of being alone..."**
**"don't mistake shame for a closed door."**

The wind passes between you.

For once, Vael adds nothing.

route_seul.title: The Road Alone
route_seul.narrator: The first days are almost easy.
route_seul.text:
You walk north.

Not toward Aurenthal.
Not toward Erevane.
Not toward the Four.

North, simply.

The world is vast when no one tells you where to go.

The black blade stays silent.

The villages are far.
The roads are empty.
The nights are cold, but bearable.

You sleep better.

Not well.

Better.

For three days, you think you have found the answer.

No Order.
No prophecy.
No eyes measuring you.

Just you.

The wind.

The road.

And the blade that no longer trembles.

silence_paix.title: Almost Peace
silence_paix.text:
Silence has a shape.

You didn't know that before.

It spreads over the hills.
It settles on the stones.
It fills the spaces the others' voices used to occupy.

Aryn asks no questions.
Taera doesn't look at your hands.
Vael makes no jokes to hide what he has understood.
Ikar doesn't watch your blade.

No one is waiting for you.

No one fears you.

Because there is no one.

You close your eyes.

For the first time since Cendral,
you breathe without feeling
that someone is counting your breaths.

premiers_bandits.title: The Bandits
premiers_bandits.narrator: The first accident comes almost silently.
premiers_bandits.text:
There are three of them.

Not soldiers.
Not monsters.
Not legendary assassins.

Three scrawny men with rusted knives
and more fear than malice in their eyes.

**"Your purse."** says the first one.

You could run.

You could talk.

You could raise your hands.

But since Cendral,
your body knows how to do something else before you do.

The black blade comes out.

Violet light strikes the trees.

A breath.

Just one.

When you open your eyes again,
the three men are on the ground.

Alive.

But one of them is screaming.

His leg is pinned under a fallen trunk.

You did not aim at the tree.

aider_bandit.title: Helping
aider_bandit.text:
You run toward him.

He sees you coming with the black blade in your hand.

His screaming changes.

It's no longer pain.

It's you.

**"No — no, don't come near—"**

You stop.

You set the blade on the ground.

You raise your hands.

**"I want to help."**

He doesn't hear you.

Or he can't.

You lift the trunk with the Chaos.

Too fast.

Violet force explodes into the earth.
Roots tear apart.
Stones fly.

The man is free.

He crawls away from you, crying.

You saved him.

He looks at you as if you had destroyed him.

partir_bandit.title: Leaving
partir_bandit.text:
You back away.

You tell yourself they attacked you.

You tell yourself it isn't your fault.

You tell yourself that if they hadn't raised their knives,
nothing would have happened.

The screaming follows you between the trees.

For a long time.

Longer than you could bear.

When it finally stops,
it's worse.

The silence has changed.

It is no longer empty.

It holds something.

trace_violette.title: The Trace
trace_violette.text:
You sleep badly.

In the morning, you go back in spite of yourself
to the place of the accident.

The earth is split.

The trees around have black marks,
but they aren't burned.

Drained.

As if the light had been pulled from their bark.

You lay your hand on a violet scar.

It's cold.

Your blade responds.

Not with words.

With a sensation.

Something like:

*I can protect you.*

You pull your hand away.

You don't know what frightens you most.

That it's false.

Or that it's true.

eviter_routes.title: Away from the Roads
eviter_routes.text:
You avoid the roads.

The villages become lights in the distance.

You watch them from the hills.

Warm windows.
Chimneys.
Voices.

People.

You stay outside.

It's better this way.

No one provokes you.
No one gets hurt.
No one sees the blade.

You eat little.
You sleep in pieces.
You speak less and less.

After a week,
you realize you haven't heard your own voice
in three days.

You try to say your name.

It sounds strange.

Like the name of someone you once knew.

village_grise.title: Griseval
village_grise.text:
The village is called Griseval.

You shouldn't have stopped.

But it's raining.
You're hungry.
And for a few hours,
you want to believe you can walk into somewhere
without the world tensing up around you.

You hide the blade under your cloak.

At the inn, no one recognizes you.

The soup is too salty.
The bread is hard.
The bench creaks.

It's the best meal of your life.

Then a little girl by the fireplace
points at your cloak.

**"Why is it glowing underneath?"**

Everyone turns toward you.

verite_auberge.title: The Truth
verite_auberge.text:
You open your cloak.

The black blade absorbs the light of the room.

The fireplace flames lean toward it.

Someone whispers:

**"Chaos."**

The word falls across the tables.

You raise your hands.

**"I don't want to hurt anyone."**

For a second,
no one moves.

Then the door bursts open.

A man runs in.

**"The wolves are in the pens!"**

The room erupts in noise.

And you,
before you even think,
rush out with them.

sortie_auberge.title: Fleeing the Inn
sortie_auberge.text:
You leave too fast.

A chair falls behind you.
Someone shouts.
The little girl is crying.

In the street, rain strikes your face.

Then you hear another cry.

Not from the inn.

Farther off.

Toward the pens.

Wolves.

Real ones.

You could leave now.

No one owes you anything.
You owe nothing to anyone.

Except that you see a figure running toward the beasts.

A child.

Too small.

Too slow.

loups_enclos.title: The Wolves
loups_enclos.text:
The wolves are not normal.

Their eyes burn with a white fever.
Their saliva steams in the rain.

An old man says:

**"Malebrume."**

You don't know what it means.

You only know the child has fallen.

A wolf leaps.

You strike.

The Chaos answers.

Too strong.

Violet light tears through the pen,
the beast,
the fence,
the barn behind.

The wolf vanishes.

The barn collapses.

People are screaming underneath.

decombres.title: Beneath the Barn
decombres.text:
You run toward the rubble.

Your blade vibrates.

It wants to finish the fight.

You ignore it.

You tear the beams away one by one.
Too fast.
Not gently enough.

Taera would have known where to put her hands.

Aryn would have said what to move first.

Vael would have found the child who isn't crying.

Ikar would have kept the wolves away from you.

But they aren't here.

You are alone.

You pull out two living people.

The third no longer moves.

Rain washes the dust from his face.

Someone behind you whispers:

**"You saved us."**

Then, lower:

**"But look around you."**

tuer_loups.title: Finishing the Fight
tuer_loups.text:
You turn toward the other wolves.

You stop thinking.

It's simpler that way.

The black blade traces violet arcs through the rain.
Each strike tears up the earth.
Each dodge breaks something.
Each breath of the Chaos widens the circle of disaster.

When the last wolf falls,
there is no pen left.

No barn.

No silence either.

Only weeping.
Shouting.
Calls from under the beams.

You won.

That's the problem.

partir_griseval.title: Don't Look Back
partir_griseval.text:
You leave.

The screams stay behind.

You tell yourself this wasn't your fight.

That every time you come near,
someone suffers.

So leaving
might be the way to help.

The rain turns the road black.

Your blade is cold against your leg.

After an hour,
you stop.

You have forgotten the taste of the soup.

You have not forgotten the child's cry.

matin_griseval.title: The Morning After
matin_griseval.text:
In the morning, Griseval counts the damage.

Three wounded.
One dead.
Two houses cracked.
The barn destroyed.
The wolves dead.

The child lives.

Her mother thanks you.

She trembles as she does it.

The village chief doesn't know where to look.

**"We know what you did."**
**"We also know what happened."**

He takes a breath.

**"Leave before the others wake up."**

No anger.

No hatred.

Just tired fear.

That's worse.

honte.title: Shame
honte.text:
You walk until you can no longer feel your legs.

Griseval vanishes behind the hills.

You saved a child.
You killed the wolves.
You prevented something worse.

And yet,
a woman died under a barn
that your power brought down.

You think back to the Four.

To their looks.
To their hands.
To their voices around the fire.

They weren't only there to watch you.

They were there to limit the damage.

To be what you are not yet.

A thought crosses your mind.

*I could go back.*

It doesn't stay long.

Shame chases it away.

You keep walking.

orage.title: The Storm
orage.text:
The storm arrives without warning.

The wind flattens the grass.
The rain strikes sideways.
Lightning strikes far off, then closer.

You find shelter under a stone arch.

The black blade lights up on its own.

Violet in the night.

You stare at it.

**"Stop."**

It doesn't stop.

Thunder answers.

Or maybe it's you.

The violet light climbs along your arm.

Not an attack.

Not yet.

An overflow.

Like a full glass that keeps being filled.

choices.text: Plant the blade in the ground.

ancrer_seul.title: Grounding Alone
ancrer_seul.text:
You plant the blade in the ground.

Just as Taera taught you.

Both hands on the hilt.
Knees in the mud.
Breathing low.

**"I am here."**

The phrase has the taste of her voice.

The earth trembles.

Not enough.

You are not Taera.
You are not the Earth.

You hold the Chaos back anyway.

Part of it sinks into the ground.
Another part stays in your bones.

By morning,
the plateau around you is split
like an old plate.

But nothing has burned.

No one was there.

It's a victory.

A victory without a witness.

laisser_sortir.title: Letting It Out
laisser_sortir.text:
You stop holding back.

For a second,
it is almost a relief.

The Chaos bursts out in a circle.

The rain vanishes before it touches the ground.
Stones shatter.
The arch above you breaks apart and rises into the sky
as if the world were falling upside down.

You scream.

Not in anger.

In exhaustion.

When everything stops,
the storm is gone.

The plateau too.

Only a crater remains.

And you, at its center.

Standing.

Unharmed.

That's what terrifies you most.

rumeurs.title: The Rumors
rumeurs.text:
Rumors travel faster than you do.

A man with a black blade.
A violet light in the mountains.
A village saved and broken.
A crater on a plateau where there had been only an arch.

You hear your own story in other people's mouths.

It changes every time.

In one version, you're a monster.
In another, a savior.
In a third, a sign of the end.

None of them says you were afraid.

None of them says you tried.

None of them says you would have wanted
someone to be there to tell you what to do next.

choices.text: Look for a place where no one lives.

caravane.title: The Caravan
caravane.text:
The caravan is attacked by raiders.

This time,
you wait.

You watch.

You choose.

Aryn would have approved.

You strike the ground in front of the horses.
Not the men.
Not the wheels.

The Chaos opens a trench between the raiders and the caravan.

Perfect.

Almost.

A horse panics.
The first cart tips over.
Crates fall.
A wheel breaks.

No one dies.

But a merchant looks at you,
his face white.

**"Thank you."**

He says it the way you'd toss a coin to a wolf
so it wanders off farther.

choices.text: Accept that this is the best possible.
Promise yourself never to help anyone again.

frontiere_neige.title: The White Frontier
frontiere_neige.text:
You reach the mountains as the snow begins.

Up there,
villages are rare.
Roads disappear.
Names too.

No one follows you.

Not the Four.
Not Erevane.
Not the rumors.

Or perhaps they still follow,
but too far away to reach you.

You find an abandoned cabin
near a cliff.

The roof barely holds.
The door creaks.
Smoke is rising from the chimney inside.

It's perfect.

Not because it's beautiful.

Because it's far away.

plus_loin.title: Even Farther
plus_loin.text:
You keep going.

Always farther.

There is something reassuring
about the idea that there is always a place
even less inhabited than the last one.

No more tracks.
No more smoke.
No more voices.

One evening, you find a cave open over the void.

The wind sings there like Vael
when he was pretending not to be sad.

You laugh.

A real laugh.

Then you stop.

Because no one heard it.

cabane.title: Far from the World
cabane.text:
The months pass.

You learn to live with little.

Making a fire without magic.
Repairing a roof.
Trapping a hare.
Recognizing the clouds that bring a storm.

The Chaos calms down.

Or it falls asleep.

You no longer know.

Sometimes you dream of the Four.

Aryn asks whether you're sleeping.
Taera puts a blanket over your shoulders.
Ikar stays near the door.
Vael tells an absurd story about a duck, a king, and a boot.

You wake with a tight throat.

The cabin is empty.

So is the black blade.

choices.text: Carve their names into the wood.

noms_bois.title: The Names
noms_bois.text:
You take Marek's carving knife.

Your hands shake.

On the table, in the worn wood of the cabin,
you carve four names.

Aryn.

The A takes time.
You want it to be right.

Ikar.

Sharper.
Like him.

Taera.

You have to pause between the two syllables.

Vael.

The V comes out crooked.
You redo it.
Twice.

Then you stay there.
The knife in your hand.
The four names in the wood.

You touch each letter.

Water doesn't scream.
Fire advances.
Earth holds.
Air passes.

Lessons you never asked for.

That you carry anyway.

You put the knife away.

You don't know why you did it.

Yes.

You know.

choices.text: Look at the names for a long time.

effacer.title: Stop Thinking
effacer.text:
You put away everything that reminds you of the others.

The pouch of earth.
A scrap of blue cloth.
A feather you don't remember keeping.
A stone blackened by fire.

You put them in a box.

Then under the floorboards.

Then you set a table on top of it.

It's ridiculous.

As if memories needed a door to get out.

That night,
you don't dream.

In the morning,
you don't know whether it's better.

You no longer quite know what *better* means.

annees.title: The Years
annees.text:
People tell stories.

That a silhouette sometimes walks along the ridges.
That storms change course.
That monsters avoid certain valleys.
That lost travelers find a fire already lit,
then no one around it.

They also say you must not go looking for the silhouette.

Not because it attacks.

Because the world around it breaks.

A bridge gives way.
An avalanche starts too early.
A river freezes in the middle of summer.

Nothing deliberate.

Never deliberate.

But people learn.

They survive better
when they keep their distance.

choices.text: See what has become of the Four.
Keep your distance from the world.

quatre_recherche.title: Those Who Search
quatre_recherche.text:
The Four search for a long time.

Aryn reads every rumor.
Taera follows the broken lands.
Ikar climbs every road where someone has seen a violet light.
Vael talks to the people who say they saw nothing.

Especially them.

For years,
they always arrive too late.

A fire still warm.
A footprint in the snow.
A table carved with five names in an empty cabin.

On the day they find the table,
no one speaks.

Not even Vael.

Especially Vael.

Taera lays her hand on your name.

Aryn closes her eyes.

Ikar goes outside.

The wind moves through the cabin.

And for once,
it carries no jokes at all.

horizon.title: The Horizon
horizon.text:
The world survives.

That is already a lot.

You look at it from a cliff
where the maps no longer have names.

The sea is below.

Gray.
Vast.
Indifferent.

Your black blade is at your belt.

It hasn't vibrated for months.

Or it vibrates so softly
that you've learned to stop telling the difference.

You take out Marek's knife.

You open it.

You close it.

There was Cendral.
There was the crossroads.
There was the escape.

There was Griseval.
The storm.
The cabin.
The names in the wood.

And now this cliff.

The wind.

The sea.

Somewhere, Aerith goes on.

The cities rebuild.
People remember.
The Four are perhaps still searching.

Or perhaps they have understood
that some paths need time.

And that some storms
end up calming down
on their own.

Slowly.

But on their own.

paix_courte.title: A Night With Nothing
paix_courte.text:
That evening you find a clearing.

Small.
Sheltered from the wind.

You make a fire.

Small.
Without magic.
With your hands.

Just as Ikar showed you.
*Fire follows intention.*

You think of him as you strike the flint.

The fire catches.

You eat.

You watch the stars.

The black blade is set down far away.

Tonight it does not vibrate.

Tonight nothing happens.

Just a fire.
Stars.
And the silence of a sleeping forest.

You think of Cendral.

Of the fires they used to light on the square in the evenings.

It's not the same.

But it's a little like it.

penser_eux_nuit.title: In the Fire
penser_eux_nuit.text:
You watch the flames.

Ikar would say the fire thinks for you.

Aryn would say the water around you listens.

Taera would say the earth beneath you holds you up.

Vael would say something funny
so that you stop hurting yourself.

They are not here.

But their voices are.

The sentences they said.
The gestures they made.

You wonder whether they are searching.

Probably.

Aryn always searches.

You stretch your legs.

The fire crackles.

You sleep better than you have in a long time.

noms_longtemps.title: Staying Here
noms_longtemps.text:
You stay seated in front of the table.

For a long time.

The names.

You think of what Aryn would have told you.
*Doubt is water. It eventually finds its way.*

That path brought you here.

To a cabin with no name.
In mountains with no maps.

With four names carved in wood.

It isn't what she imagined.

It isn't what you imagined either.

But the names are there.

And that means something.

Something you can't yet put into words.

Maybe someday.
